text: Only non-empty lists are valid arguments: the empty list has no first or last element, so it is outside the assumption and the behaviour on it is unconstrained.

phrase: return a copy of the given array
text: The empty list is not covered, because the sum of its first and last index values is undefined; the function may raise (for example an IndexError) or return anything on it.
Only the cases the condition names constrain the order; where the text is cut off (after "or sort it") the order of the returned list is unconstrained.
Only the contents of the returned list matter; returning the argument object itself is acceptable as long as it holds the required elements.

phrase: first index value, last index value
text: The index numbers themselves: 0 + (len(array) - 1), so the parity depends only on the length of the array.

phrase: the sum( first index value, last index value)
text: The first and last elements of the array after sorting, that is its minimum plus its maximum.
For a one-element array the single element is counted once, so the sum is that element.
Strictly increasing order, so duplicate values are removed; this contradicts returning a copy of the given array.
When the sum is even, the returned list is in descending (non-increasing) order, the usual counterpart of the ascending case.
